svg.title: How Washington built the category that now holds two Palestine solidarity organisations
svg.desc: A bilingual chart of the American designation machinery that led to the Treasury action of 26 August 2026. The timeline runs from 15 October 2024, when the United States and Canada jointly sanctioned the Samidoun Palestinian Prisoner Solidarity Network as a front for the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, itself designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization in 1997; through National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 of 25 September 2025 on countering domestic terrorism and organized political violence; the State Department's designation on 20 November 2025 of Antifa Ost in Germany, the Informal Anarchist Federation and International Revolutionary Front in Italy, and Armed Proletarian Justice and Revolutionary Class Self-Defense in Greece, the first designations of groups tied to anti-fascist activism abroad; the White House 2026 Counterterrorism Strategy released on 6 May 2026, which names violent left-wing extremists as one of three principal threat families beside narcoterrorists and Islamist groups; Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visa restriction policy announced on 16 July 2026, which denies visas to foreign nationals who have participated in economic sabotage or financed, recruited or provided logistical support for violent or criminal actions; and the Office of Foreign Assets Control designation on 26 August 2026 of Palestine Action, Masar Badil, Autistici Inventati and two Masar Badil officials, Zaid Abdulnasser in Germany and Rawa Alsagheer in Brazil, under Executive Order 13224. A second panel sets out what a Specially Designated Global Terrorist listing does: property blocked, United States persons barred from transactions, strict liability under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, criminal exposure under the material support statute at 18 United States Code section 2339B, and bank de-risking, with no criminal charge and no court finding required and delisting available only by administrative petition to the Office of Foreign Assets Control. A third panel records the British track for Palestine Action: proscribed on 5 July 2025 after a break-in at RAF Brize Norton on 20 June 2025, more than 3,000 arrests connected to support for the group by mid-June 2026, the High Court quashing the ban on 13 February 2026, the Court of Appeal restoring it on 15 June 2026, and the Supreme Court granting permission to appeal in early August 2026.
